note: Every purchase is either official (Credit Score debt, traced) or street (physical cash at a black-market markup, untraced). Credit is the leash the system uses to keep the lower classes compliant: fine for groceries and rent, ruinous for anything that matters on a job.

official.scrutinyNote: How much attention an official purchase draws. Higher = the system makes you pay for it in compliance.
official.override: An entry may set cost.scoreOverride to replace the formula (a number), or null to make it cash only. Overrides beat the rarity rule.
official.trace: Official purchases are logged against the character's identity.
official.blackMarketNote: The two rarest tiers never appear in official shops: street cash only.

cash.note: Street purchases cost the listed Cr price x1 (no markup) to x10 in physical cash. The GM sets the markup for the whole table (owner 2026-11-14); x3 when nobody set it.

magazine.note: Decision 55: a spare magazine for a gun costs 10% of the gun (minimum 5 Cr). Every gun bought comes with 2. Reload uses one; the partly used one is discarded.

sell.note: Selling gives half the list price in cash; gear bought officially (registered) only a quarter — resale is allowed, but corporate planned obsolescence makes it worth little (decision 57). Street-bought units are sold first. Custom items: the player types the amount. Hot goods (decision 345: a looted tracked weapon, a traced item) fetch a quarter: the fence takes the risk.

washer.note: A fixer turns cash into Credit Score (fake salaries) or Credit Score into cash (borrowing against your score). The GM makes each offer; these are the form's starting values (decision 143). A hot gun (decision 345): the fixer takes share % of its list price; a d20 at or under risk and the trail leads back to the crew.

essentials.note: Owner 2026-11-14: the market's first tab — the most basic gear covering every base before going out (one each). Not specialist tools (lockpicks, RFID kits). role → shop.ess.<role> (why it's there).

carry.note: Owner 2026-11-18: bulky things (two-handed weapons, anything marked bulky) — everyone carries freeBulky without trouble; one bag (bulkyRoom) adds its room; more than that and you are Slowed until you put something down.

bodyLoot.note: Decision 345: a fallen enemy's weapon drops usable by its rarity (percent; rolled when the body is made). Junk always; the best almost never — a truly remarkable event.

haggle.note: Owner 2026-11-18 (decision 346): one roll to move a price. The player picks how hard to push (each step a % and a difficulty step) and how: an honest haggle, working the street, or a swindle (double the %, but a failure burns the deal). A natural 20 makes it worse by fumblePct. The GM can set the other side's mood: easy −1 step, tough +1. At the market it lasts the trip (until the next scene).
